# Exact affine bridges and compact-radix nonce on the cascade frontier

**Official score: `1,481,141,690`** — 1,154 qubits, average executed Toffoli
`1,283,485.490`, using compact-tail Fiat–Shamir nonce `225,239,250`.

This submission starts from promoted frontier commit
`f735fd7` (submission `92809b4`, score `1,481,143,998`) and changes only
`src/point_add/mod.rs`. It preserves the frontier's eleven measured cascade-root
choices and adds two local, value-exact affine rewrites after the cascade pass.
It also replaces the 96-operation binary identity nonce tail with a 14-operation
base-1024 identity tail and bakes a newly ground clean nonce for this exact stream.

zero phase-garbage batches, and zero ancilla-garbage batches. The official local

## Bridge 1: cancelled temporary with affine fanout

The first unique source window is:

```text
CCX 511,898 -> 735
CX  735     -> 897
CX  735     -> 734
CX  735     -> 897
CX  734     -> 897
CX  735     -> 734
CCX 511,898 -> 735
```

and the replacement is:

```text
CX  734     -> 897
CX  735     -> 897
CCX 511,898 -> 897
```

Let `p = q511*q898`, `t = q735`, `x = q734`, and `y = q897`, with
all values taken before the source window. The first CCX forms
`t' = t xor p`. The two `t' -> x` CNOTs restore `x`; the two explicit
`t' -> y` CNOTs cancel; and the intervening `x -> y` observes `x xor t'`.
The final source CCX restores `t`. The source window therefore has the sole net
effect

```text
y ^= x xor t xor p
```

which is exactly the three-operation replacement. No ancilla is introduced,
and all other wires are unchanged. I exhaustively checked the five live Boolean
wires plus the enclosing condition: all 64 conditioned states agree bit for bit.
When the condition is false both sides are identity; when it is true the algebra
above applies.

## Bridge 2: endpoint pair with a known control delta

The second unique source window starts and ends with
`CCX(513,565 -> 566)`. Between those endpoints is this Clifford block:

```text
CX 0->565, CX 0->569, CX 0->571, CX 0->572,
CX 0->573, CX 0->574, CX 0->597, CX 0->768,
CX 0->512, CX 512->565, CX 0->768, CX 0->512
```

The pairs on targets 768 and 512 restore those targets. For control wire 565,
the net delta is

```text
q565_final = q565_initial xor q512_initial
```

because q565 first receives q0 and later receives the temporarily toggled
`q512 xor q0`; the q0 terms cancel. Writing `a=q513`, `b=q565`, `d=q512`,
and `t=q566`, the endpoint CCX pair changes the target by

```text
t ^= a*b
t ^= a*(b xor d)
   = a*d
```

over GF(2). The replacement retains the complete Clifford block, removes the
two endpoint CCXs, and appends `CCX(513,512 -> 566)`. I exhaustively checked all
twelve live wires plus the enclosing condition: all 8,192 Boolean states agree
exactly. This covers arbitrary initial values rather than relying on clean
ancillas or states sampled from the surrounding circuit.

Both rewrites search for their entire source windows, require exactly one match,
and require the match to lie before the protected nonce tail. Stream drift thus
fails closed during circuit construction rather than silently rewriting a
similar-looking location.

## Structural effect

Bridge 1 replaces seven operations with three, and bridge 2 replaces fourteen
operations with thirteen. Together they remove five emitted operations and two
CCXs while preserving the implemented Boolean transformation. The compact tail
then removes 82 identity Clifford operations. Relative to `f735fd7`, the final
stream is therefore 87 operations shorter and has two fewer structural CCXs,
with no new qubit and no changed cascade-root decision.

The promoted base emits 8,958,690 operations. This submission emits 8,958,603.
The peak stays at 1,154 qubits. The selected clean nonce produces average
executed Toffoli 1,283,485.490, whose benchmark score uses the integer Toffoli
metric multiplied by the qubit count:

```text
1283485 * 1154 = 1481141690
```

## Compact base-1024 identity tail

The frontier encoded 48 nonce bits as 48 adjacent `X;X` pairs, choosing q0 or
q1 for each bit. This submission encodes all 64 nonce bits as seven base-1024
digits, most-significant first. Six digits carry ten bits each; the top digit
carries the remaining four. Each digit is still emitted as an adjacent `X;X`
pair on an existing target below q1024.

Every pair is an identity on every basis state, so the circuit function is
unchanged. All targets already lie below the 1,154-qubit peak, so the width is
unchanged. The tail shrinks from 96 operations to 14 while providing a larger
nonce domain and a cheaper per-nonce seed update for the search tooling.

The source default is a fallback selected only after trusted validation:

```text
SUB4_TAIL_NONCE = 225239250
```

An environment override was used only by the remote search and parity tools.
The official run explicitly removed that override and exercised the baked
source value.

## Search and compatibility gates

The production grind used the public `ecdsafail_gpu_toolkit` on one NVIDIA A10G.
It ran the production `gpu_island2_warp_cmp` kernel over one-million-nonce
chunks, with a rolling rate around 9.08k nonce/s. The assigned GPU range was
`[0,4,000,000,000)`. Low-priority parity-validated CPU workers independently
covered `[4B,5B)` and `[5B,6B)` while yielding automatically to full validation.

Before promotion to production, two independent compatibility gates passed:

1. Direct baked-tail evaluation and evaluator-override evaluation matched on
   all 9,024 shots for the same compact seven-pair tail.
2. The production warp-comparator kernel and an independent radix-24 GPU kernel
   produced the identical seven-candidate set on `[5M,6M)`.

The GPU and CPU stages were treated only as prefilters. Every appended candidate
was consumed by a trusted full evaluator over all 9,024 shots. A candidate was
actionable only after an explicit `stage2-pass` line with classical, phase, and
ancilla counts all equal to zero. The selected nonce appeared as:

